items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Most names are clear (createRestoredQueryState, reconcileRestoredQueryState), but resolveRestoredData uses 4-deep nested ternaries with primary/secondary fallbacks and no comments, so the intent is hard to follow.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Restore types, marker and helpers sit in query.ts, not a separate persister.ts. Bulk restore calls existingQuery.setState from outside instead of a reducer action. The default QueryState literal is hand-copied in createPersister. Extra helper exported publicly.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: isInfiniteDataShape treats any data with a `pages` array as infinite data and may rewrite it. PersisterRestoreState has `data?: TData | unknown`, which weakens typing. Counts and timestamps are not normalized the way the reference does. Errors are not swallowed.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: Marker is a symbol, the helper is exported, and fetch returns before success callbacks. But state is applied with `this.setState(restoredState)`, not a dedicated reducer action, and bulk restore mutates existingQuery.setState from outside. The two paths share only createRestoredQueryState.

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: The plain-data fetch path still works and the new exports are additive. Bulk restore changed from setQueryData(updatedAt) to queryCache.build plus setState even for plain persisted entries, an internal behaviour change. The QueryPersister type was widened.
